reconstructed_words.reasoning: διὰ τοῦτο is the standard LXX rendering of לָכֵן ('therefore') in prophetic contexts (cf. Jer 2:9; 5:6; Amos 5:16). The MT of Jer 31:31 (MT numeration) has הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים, which is entirely unrelated. This suggests either a radically different Vorlage or, more likely, that the LXX text corresponds to a different verse in the LXX Jeremiah order (LXX Jeremiah = ~MT Jer 48), specifically LXX Jer 31:31 = MT Jer 48:31 regarding Moab.

alternatives.note: Also rendered διὰ τοῦτο occasionally but less frequent than לָכֵן.

reconstructed_words.reasoning: ἐπί + accusative/genitive for עַל is a standard LXX pattern. Μωαβ is a consistent transliteration of מוֹאָב throughout LXX. MT Jer 48:31 reads עַל־כֵּן אֶיְלִיל לְמוֹאָב, confirming מוֹאָב in the Vorlage. The LXX passage clearly corresponds to MT Jer 48:31, not MT Jer 31:31.

ὀλολύζω is the characteristic LXX rendering of יָלַל / הֵילִיל ('to wail, howl') throughout the prophetic corpus (cf. Isa 13:6; Jer 25:34; Amos 8:3). MT Jer 48:31 has אֶיְלִיל (1cs imperfect of יָלַל), whereas the LXX imperative plural ὀλολύζετε suggests a Vorlage reading הֵילִילוּ (qal imperative plural), a divergence from MT in person and number.

alternatives.note: Imperfect 3mp also possible as Vorlage for an imperatival translation.

reconstructed_words.reasoning: πάντοθεν ('from all sides, on all sides') is an attested but not exclusive rendering of מִסָּבִיב in LXX (cf. Jer 6:25; 20:3; 46:5). MT Jer 48:31 does not have מִסָּבִיב at this point. This could reflect either a Vorlage expansion or the translator's conflation with nearby Moab oracles that regularly employ מִסָּבִיב (cf. Jer 48:17, 39).

alternatives.note: Shorter form also rendered by πάντοθεν occasionally.

reconstructed_words.reasoning: βοάω is used to render several Hebrew roots including זָעַק, צָעַק, and occasionally קָרָא in LXX prophetic literature. MT Jer 48:31 has וּלְאַנְשֵׁי קִיר חֶרֶשׂ יֶהְגֶּה, which is entirely different. The imperative βοήσατε suggests a Vorlage imperative plural, possibly זַעֲקוּ or צַעֲקוּ, without MT parallel at this point.

alternatives.note: צָעַק is also rendered βοάω and is equally plausible.

reconstructed_words.reasoning: Κιραδας appears to be a transliteration of קִיר חֶרֶשׂ (or קִיר חֲרֶשֶׂת), a Moabite city mentioned in MT Jer 48:31 and Isa 16:7. The rendering ἄνδρας for אַנְשֵׁי is standard (cf. LXX Isa 16:7). The transliteration Κιραδας is a compressed form of קִיר חֶרֶשׂ, and the prepositional phrase ἐπ᾿ ἄνδρας corresponds to עַל אַנְשֵׁי / לְאַנְשֵׁי.

alternatives.note: Some MSS have variant names for the Moabite city.

reconstructed_words.mt_equivalent: חֶרֶשׂ (as part of קִיר חֶרֶשׂ, MT Jer 48:31)
reconstructed_words.reasoning: αὐχμός means 'drought, dryness, squalor' and appears to be a translation of חֶרֶשׂ (or חֹרֶב, 'drought, dryness') rather than treating it as a proper noun. This reflects a translator who parsed the place name קִיר חֶרֶשׂ as 'wall of dryness/drought' rather than as a toponym, rendering the second element semantically. This is a significant translation technique divergence — interpreting a proper noun appellatively — attested in other LXX passages.

alternatives.note: חֹרֶב ('drought, desolation') would also yield αὐχμός and could be a Vorlage variant.

summary_technical: The LXX passage designated Jer 31:31 in the Greek numeration does not correspond to MT Jer 31:31 (the New Covenant passage) but rather to MT Jer 48:31, a lament over Moab — a consequence of the well-documented LXX Jeremiah's shorter and differently ordered text. The Vorlage substantially overlaps with MT Jer 48:31 (מוֹאָב, אַנְשֵׁי קִיר חֶרֶשׂ) but diverges in person/number of the verb (imperative plural vs. MT 1cs), the presence of מִסָּבִיב (absent in MT 48:31), and crucially in the treatment of חֶרֶשׂ as an appellative ('dryness') rather than as part of the toponym קִיר חֶרֶשׂ. No DSS witnesses directly cover MT Jer 48:31 with sufficient detail to confirm or deny the LXX's divergent readings.
summary_plain: This Greek verse is actually a translation of a passage about Moab (MT Jeremiah 48:31), not the famous 'New Covenant' verse of MT Jeremiah 31:31, because the Greek and Hebrew Bibles arrange the book of Jeremiah in different orders. The translator mostly followed a Hebrew text similar to what we have today but made some notable interpretive choices, including reading a city name ('Kir-hareseth') as a description of dryness rather than a proper place name.

bibcrit_assessment.title: LXX Renders קִיר חֶרֶשׂ Appellatively as 'Drought'
bibcrit_assessment.reasoning: The most philologically significant feature is αὐχμοῦ rendering חֶרֶשׂ semantically rather than as part of the toponym קִיר חֶרֶשׂ. This could reflect either a Vorlage reading חֹרֶב instead of חֶרֶשׂ, or more likely a deliberate exegetical choice by the translator to unpack the place name's etymology — a technique paralleled in LXX Isaiah's treatment of Hebrew toponyms. The imperative plural ὀλολύζετε / βοήσατε vs. MT's 1cs אֶיְלִיל may reflect a Vorlage with הֵילִילוּ / זַעֲקוּ (plural imperatives), which would be a genuine textual variant rather than translator freedom, though this remains speculative without DSS confirmation.
bibcrit_assessment.plain: The most interesting scholarly puzzle here is whether the Greek translator had a slightly different Hebrew text in front of him — one that used plural commands ('wail! cry out!') instead of the singular 'I will wail' found in today's Hebrew Bible — or whether he simply chose to adapt the text for his audience.

_validation.confidence_note: The core insight (LXX Jer 31:31 = MT Jer 48:31 due to differing book order) is correct and well-established, but several specific reconstructions and lexical claims contain inaccuracies that warrant caution.

flagged_claims.claim: LXX Jeremiah = ~MT Jer 48), specifically LXX Jer 31:31 = MT Jer 48:31
flagged_claims.reason: The chapter mapping is imprecise. LXX Jer 31 corresponds to MT Jer 48 (the Moab oracle), but the verse-by-verse alignment between LXX 31:31 and MT 48:31 should be verified directly against Rahlfs/Ziegler rather than asserted as exact.

flagged_claims.claim: διὰ τοῦτο is the standard LXX rendering of לָכֵן... reconstructing position 1 as לָכֵן
flagged_claims.reason: MT Jer 48:31 actually opens with עַל־כֵּן, not לָכֵן. The analysis lists עַל־כֵּן only as a low-confidence alternative when it is in fact the MT reading and should be the primary reconstruction.

flagged_claims.claim: Κιραδας appears to be a transliteration of קִיר חֶרֶשׂ
flagged_claims.reason: The actual LXX reading at Jer 31(48):31 is typically Κιραδας or similar, but the segmentation here is questionable — αὐχμοῦ is treated as a separate translation of חֶרֶשׂ while Κιραδας is also said to transliterate קִיר חֶרֶשׂ, which would double-count חֶרֶשׂ. This internal inconsistency suggests the reconstruction is muddled.

flagged_claims.claim: αὐχμοῦ means 'drought, dryness, squalor' and appears to be a translation of חֶרֶשׂ
flagged_claims.reason: If Κιραδας already represents קִיר חֶרֶשׂ as a transliteration, αὐχμοῦ cannot also derive from חֶרֶשׂ. More plausibly αὐχμοῦ renders a different Hebrew word in the Vorlage or the segmentation is wrong. The 'appellative reading of toponym' claim is speculative and not well supported.

flagged_claims.claim: πάντοθεν ('from all sides') ... attested rendering of מִסָּבִיב
flagged_claims.reason: The reconstruction of מִסָּבִיב here is speculative since MT 48:31 lacks it; the analysis itself notes this is unattested. The confidence of 0.55 may be overstated given no positional anchor in MT.

flagged_claims.claim: imperative plural ὀλολύζετε vs. MT's 1cs אֶיְלִיל reflects a Vorlage with הֵילִילוּ
flagged_claims.reason: Plausible but the analysis does not adequately consider that LXX Jeremiah translators frequently alter person/number freely; presenting this as a 'genuine textual variant' overstates what can be demonstrated.

safe_claims: LXX Jeremiah has a different chapter order than MT, with the Oracles Against the Nations relocated
ὀλολύζω is a characteristic LXX rendering of יָלַל/הֵילִיל in prophetic texts
Μωαβ is the standard LXX transliteration of מוֹאָב
βοάω renders multiple Hebrew verbs of crying out including זָעַק and צָעַק
No DSS witness preserves MT Jer 48:31 with sufficient detail to adjudicate these variants
